To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
actin and microtubules cooperate in the positioning and movement of centrosomes in human leukocytes exposed to TPA.
the actin network is involved in the positioning of the centrosomes and in their motility.
the actin cytoskeleton and microtubules interact to determine the position of the cell's microtubule-organizing center (MTOC) and that this interaction may involve the centrioles themselves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic relationship between actin and microtubules, and with the role of the cytoskeleton in positioning the centrosome and in cell locomotion.
the mechanisms of cell spreading, centrosome splitting, and aster motility.
the role of actin filaments in the positioning and movement of centriolar asters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
actin is involved in the positioning and movement of the centrosomes in human neutrophils.
the TPA-induced cell spreading and centrosome splitting are both dependent on intact actin microfilaments, which in turn may be necessary for the proper functioning of the microtubule cytoskeleton.
the actin microfilament network is a major determinant of the position of the microtubule-based organelles in the cytoplasm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the actin network is a major determinant of the position of centrosomes, and the microtubular network is a major force in moving the centrosome.
the centrosome/aster complexes, which are normally immobile, are induced by TPA to move in response to a change in the actin/microtubule relationship.
actin plays a role in the positioning and in the motility of the centrosomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoskeleton is a dynamic entity that is constantly changing in response to external stimuli.
the centrosome is a highly dynamic organelle that can be moved around in the cytoplasm by microtubule-dependent actin-based forces.
actin is a critical component of the machinery that controls centrosome position and movement.
